Sar-e-Hussain Kata Hai Jiss Ibteda Ke Liye.
Hai Be Rida Sar-e-Zainab Oss Inteha Ke Liye.

1
Bataya Hur Ne Yeh Parh Kar Hussain Ka Kalma.
Keh Ya Hussain Zarori Hai La Illah Ke Liye.
Charha Ke Bano Ne Nani Si Aastino Ko.
Sanwara Hai Ali Asghar Ko Bhi Waga Ke Liye.

2
Abhi Hai Khaimay Ke Dar Par Khari Hoi Zainab.
Abhi Na Halq Pe Khanjar Chala Khuda Ke Liye.
Sakina Teri Khamoshi Peh Hai Bapa Kohram.
Tars Raha Hai Yeh Zindaan Teri Sada Ke Liye.

3
Pisar Ke Seene Se Haye Wo Khainch Kar Barchi.
Uthana Shah Ka Hathoon Ko Wo Dua Ke Liye.
 Navaid Sani-e-Zahra Se Maang Un Ka Karam.
Safina Chahiye Iss Qulzam-e-Sana Ke Liye.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/sar-e-hussain-kata-hai-jiss-ibteda-ke-liye-tajpoints-051d56749ba1c857cba4.md')
_, metadata, body = p.read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = metadata.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1]
for edition, numerals in [(roman, '123'), (body, '۱۲۳')]:
    blocks = edition.strip().split('\\n\\n')
    lines = [[line.strip() for line in block.splitlines()] for block in blocks]
    assert [len(block) for block in lines] == [2, 5, 5, 5]
    assert [block[0] for block in lines[1:]] == list(numerals)
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print('Both editions have a two-verse opening and three four-verse stanzas.')
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 14 verses in Urdu script and retained the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`, normalizing capitalization and removing verse-final periods. Verified that both versions have a two-verse opening and three four-verse stanzas.

Set the Urdu title and right-to-left direction, kept the Roman alternate title, and removed the resolved `noUrdu` tag. I read the ambiguous Roman *waga* as **وغا** (“battle”).
